newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Albanian paralysis outbreak caused by polio - WHO.
newsitem.headline: Albanian paralysis outbreak caused by polio - WHO.

text.p: A mysterious outbreak of paralytic disease in Albania earlier this year, which some reports linked to a mass immunisation campaign, was due to poliomyelitis, the World Health Organisation said on Wednesday.
It warned that visitors to Albania should ensure they were immunised against polio.

The U.N. agency said the polio virus in the outbreak -- which has so far killed seven people with 59 other cases reported -- had been identified by tests carried out in WHO laboratories in Italy and the Netherlands.
"With these new laboratory results, we can now firmly say that there is no link between the campaign and the outbreak," Dr Harry Hull of WHO's Expanded Programme on Immunisation said in a statement.
The outbreak started in April in the northwestern part of Albania and then spread to the capital, Tirana, and the rest of the country.

Initial Albanian press reports linked it to a drive sponsored by the Geneva-based WHO and the U.N. Children's Fund UNICEF to immunise 350,000 children under the age of five against polio -- one of the main childhood killers in poorer countries.
Hull said the campaign had clearly protected children during the outbreak, and only five of the 66 recorded cases were aged under five. The vast majority were teenagers and adults.
UNICEF's regional advisor on health Dr Bruno Martin supported Hull's remarks, according to the WHO statement.

"The spring campaign has protected children under five," he said. "The outbreak, which claimed an unusually high number of adults, shows that mass vaccination is effective and necessary in order to protect children from a life-threatening or disabling disease."

WHO said the two agencies, partners in a global campaign to eradicate polio, were now seeking international support for another mass immunisation campaign in Albania and were helping to organise a similar drive in neighbouring or nearby states.

"We have to move fast," the statement quoted Dr George Oblapenko of the WHO's Regional Office for Europe as saying. The new campaign would have to cover mostly the adult population because that was where the majority of cases were, he added.

One round of the campaign would need about 3,2 million doses at a cost of $300,000. "In the meantime, visitors to Albania should ensure that they are adequately immunised against polio before they depart," Oblapenko said.
WHO said that UNICEF and the business organisation Rotary International were helping organise mass immunisation campaigns in Yugoslavia, Moldova, Romania and Ukraine over the next month.
It said the two U.N. agencies believed it was vital in the drive to eradicate polio by the year 2000 to conduct large-scale operations in neighbouring countries simultaneously.

Before the Albanian outbreak, there had been only 11 confirmed cases of the disease in WHO's European region in 1996, 10 of which were in Turkey and one in Ukraine, against 206 in 1995, the health body said.
